steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Really? It's already been sent?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mmhm. Handed a printed copy to the Messenger just this morning, and he took off with it right away. Now it's all up to the reviewers' feedback whether the journal picks it up.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Thank you so much, Closure — I mean, Advisor!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh jeez, don't call me that. I'm nowhere near qualified to give you advice in your own field. The best I could do was help you sort through your ideas.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Umm...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: But you're the one who gave me the idea of writing this paper in the first place!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Sure, but I just figured it'd be a waste letting a gem like you go undiscovered.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: You also steered me in the right direction while I was writing it!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I mean, yeah, it's the first academic paper you've ever written. Of course you'd need some pointers.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: You even helped me put the finishing touches on it last night!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Snowsant, when you put it that way, I—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Yawns)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: —Don't feel so sleepy anymore.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I know you're a self-taught prodigy and all, and that you've always buried yourself in your research without paying much attention to academic journals and stuff...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But putting me down as the lead author? Really? Was that like a trap so you could say I plagiarized you?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I-I didn't think the order of the authors mattered. So, as a way of showing my gratitude, I—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm the corresponding author, thank you very much! My name goes after!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: *sniffles*...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And let's not even get into all the punctuation errors, mixed up heading levels, poorly marked citations, just dumping all the references at the end...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If it's gonna be like this next time, I'll have to start charging an editing fee! One thousand LMD per word!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I'm sorry!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Lastly, can you tell why, just why, you sent it to me...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Lets out a pained yawn)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: ...Handwritten?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No one even accepts handwritten manuscripts these days! I spent half the night just typing it all out so I could proofread it, and the other half trying to squeeze in all those charts and diagrams somehow!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: But I calculated the price of paper and ink, and found that printing it would be two LMD more expensive than writing it by hand...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Clutches her head with both hands)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Snowsant, correct me if I'm wrong, but you wanna be a great scientist, right?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And to be a great scientist, you have to publish a lot of papers, right?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Mhm. That's what you told me.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And do you realize that there are expenses other than paper and ink?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Such as?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Publication fees.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Publication fees? H-How much?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Depends on the journal, but it's always at least four figures.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: F-F-F-F-Four figures???

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: L-L-L-Let me figure out what expenses I can cut...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Takes out her tablet)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (First, I can't touch the money that's supposed to be sent home...)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Then, there are the self-research topics... Right now, there are three items...)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Lets out a long yawn)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I wouldn't worry about it too much—

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (No, I can't move around the funds I've already allocated for the projects either...)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Snowsant?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (The only area I can afford to cut is food expenses... Waah...)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Are you listening?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Fine, whatever.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If you're gonna be like this, I'm gonna catch me some shut-eye. I've got a meeting with Kal'tsit in ten minutes.
Closure casually grabs a nearby book and drapes it over her face before slumping back into her chair and letting out even, rhythmic snores.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (I don't know even know when this fee is due... But if I can have it pushed back, maybe I can scrounge up enough money...)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Um, C-Closure...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: She's asleep?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Snowsant?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Is Closure asleep?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Um, yes... It's all my fault...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I don't think you did anything wrong.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Things never go right the first time. As long as you apologize and don't make the same mistakes next time, it'll be fine. That's what Liskarm always tells me, anyway.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Mm... Thank you...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Sorry for bringing you all the way to the cafeteria just to drink plain water with me.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: So, were you looking for Closure for something?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: There's something wrong with my communications terminal, but Engineering's had its hands full of late. If I went through the standard channels, it'd take three whole months to get it fixed.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Yesterday I finally mustered the courage to head to Lutra to ask Mayer for help, but she's also really busy...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: So I made up my mind to report the problem to Closure directly... but she was asleep.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Is it serious?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Well, it's not like it's unusable. The main issue is that the signal gets choppy sometimes, but Engineering's been pushing it back because it's low priority.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Have you tried taking it apart? If it's a bad connection or something along those lines, maybe you could fix it yourself.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm afraid of breaking the parts inside...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Um, maybe I can give it a try?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Really? You'd do that for me?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: If it's not something I can handle on my own, I'll just put it back together, so don't worry.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You fixed it already?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: There was a small metal component in its Originium circuitry that rusted, so I replaced it. You shouldn't have any more issues with choppiness.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Here you go!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woah... Let me give it a try.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Umm...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Is something wrong?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I want to test it, but I'm not sure who to call... I wouldn't want to bother anyone.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Why not just... pick one at random?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I-I'll figure something out.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Umm... Is this Liskarm?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Yes... My terminal's been fixed...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It's not cutting out at all... or making any static...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Oh right, now I won't have to guess whether Franka's being serious or just joking around...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sounds good!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Mmhmm! Bye!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Thanks again, Snowsant. How much do I owe you?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Huh? Umm...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Let's not worry about that... It was just a tiny metal part, and I basically recycled it from the Engineering Department. It's not like I had to buy it or anything...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Materials are one thing, but your labor is another.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Just now, Liskarm mentioned that she'll go to you if she needs a terminal fixed. More people might need things fixed too, so we can't have you going into the red for them.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I think you should charge something. It's only fair.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (More people... Need things fixed... Charge something... It's only fair...)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (The publication fees!)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Th-Th-Then... I'll take you up on that!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Breathes deeply)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Then... How about twenty LMD?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Twenty?!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But didn't you say your publication fee was in the four-digit range?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I know it isn't much, but high volume with low margins is the best way of doing business. Nobody would come if I charged too much...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: So, twenty is enough. Twenty is just right.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Phew... That takes care of everything.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Now, to check the tags...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: These two terminals belong to Liskarm and Kroos.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: There's also Vanilla's pet water dispenser, and Instructor Dur-nar's calculator.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Including Jessica's terminal from yesterday, that makes a total of five times twenty.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: So, that's a hundred LMD in one day. Making money this way... seems pretty fast?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: A four-figure publication fee... Assuming it's just five thousand, then the amount I've earned today would be—

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: One-fiftieth...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I need to work harder.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: But I wonder why all these communication terminals have the same problem?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Mine doesn't though. How strange.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Who is it? Come in.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It's me, Jessica.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Hi there. I've finished repairing everything, so you can take them back now.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sounds good!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: This is what we owe you. One hundred LMD.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: You're paying me now? What if there still are problems...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Instructor Dur-nar said that making you do minor repair jobs is selling your abilities short.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Oh! Um, tell her I appreciate that!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Then, er, thank you for the payment.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Oh, by the way, why do all your terminals have the same point of failure? Is there some kind of design flaw?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I asked Liskarm, and she thinks they sacrificed reliability for performance, and used relatively rust-prone materials in the circuitry...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Which I guess would be the component you mentioned.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: It wouldn't be a problem under ordinary conditions, but operators often have to work in hot or humid environments, so the terminals break down faster.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: And is there no way to make it work without that part?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I don't know... Not even Closure could do anything about it, after all.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Oh right, Instructor Dur-nar asked me to tell you one more thing.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: She said it's fine to have you work on minor stuff like water dispensers and calculators, but it's best for Engineering to handle standard-issue things like the terminals.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Why's that?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: As a policy, Engineering doesn't want us doing private maintenance on standard-issue equipment. Repairing things using inconsistent materials will just make future maintenance more expensive.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Wh-What do I do then? Should I talk to Instructor Dur-nar...?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: She said she'd turn a blind eye to it, given your circumstances and the fact that Engineering has such a back-log these days.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: She just wanted to remind you to use your own judgment.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Lets out a long sigh)

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: So, next time someone asks you to fix their terminal, would you still agree to it?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I guess I'll use my own judgment.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Orchid's fountain pen, twenty LMD.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Hibiscus's food processor, twenty LMD.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: April's music player, twenty LMD—but it took two LMD to replace the buttons, and another one to replace the exposed headphone cable so she doesn't notice anything. So, that's a net of seventeen LMD.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Durin's nail clippers...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Even an amateur could reassemble a nail clipper, so I won't charge anything for that.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Altogether, that's only fifty-seven LMD this week...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: What do I do? If business continues to be this bad, I won't be able to make five thousand...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Plus, how much time do I even have to come up with the publication fee?
Snowsant lies down on the chair, involuntarily glancing at the eight terminals sitting on the table, awaiting repairs.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: If I fix all of them, that'd be a hundred-sixty LMD!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: No, no. It was one thing when I didn't know about the regulations, it's another to knowingly break the rules...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: But, the publication fee...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: *sob*... I don't want money to be the first stumbling block on my way to becoming a great scientist.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Hmm, what if I replace the structure of the Originium circuit entirely, and find a workaround that doesn't use metal parts at all? Would that still violate the regulations?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: But how could I manage something not even Closure could?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: No, I have to give it a shot. For the publication fee.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I'll repair everyone else's terminals using the old method first, then use my own to fiddle with the Originium circuitry.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: You can do it, Snowsant! You have to do it, so you can get your papers published, become a great scientist, and afford to have three meals a day... with dessert!

spans.text: You can do it, Snowsant! You
to do it, so you can get your papers published, become a great scientist, and afford to have three meals a day... with dessert!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Work... Projects... Things to fix... Everything looks good.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: It's one o'clock, huh?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Maybe I'll stay up a bit later tonight... Need to investigate how the circuitry in the terminal is connected.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: It's only 10:30, and I'm already done with all my work. Guess I was pretty lucky today.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Now, time to take a look at that circuitry.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Can't connect it like this, or like this...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ugh, I've already spent weeks on the circuitry alone.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: But if I try using this—

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Wait, I haven't worked on today's research project yet. I've got to take care of that first.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Phew... Haah...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I have a good feeling about this one. The connection might just work.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Time to pull an all-nighter!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Huh? You want me to grab all the terminals you've already fixed? You're going to go over them all again?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: It's because I found a new way to connect the circuitry, a simpler way that bypasses the need for the metal part that rusts easily.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Not even Closure could figure it out!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Hmm, now that you mention it... I guess so?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Let me try to remember whose terminals you fixed...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I've kept the receipts, so we can go off of that.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Me, Liskarm, Kroos...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Oh right, considering this is an upgrade, you can't just charge the same twenty LMD, right?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: True. Since I decided to make this change on my own, I can't ask for your money at all.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Huh?
Well, aren't you just a saint, Snowsant?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Heheh...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: That's right! She's been hard at work fixing up the terminals for how many days now? How can she not charge a cent for them—

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: C-C-Closure?!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wow, I'm here for two seconds and I'm already hearing all about your under-the-table dealings.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Jessica, since you're only an accomplice, head back to the dorms for now. I need to have a word with the prime suspect first.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Y-Yes, ma'am!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Snowsant?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What, so scared you can't walk?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: ...N-No, that's not it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Then come on in and let's have a chat.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Close the door.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: First of all, let me ask: how are your personal projects and daily work going? How much are you letting this side gig get in the way?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I-It's not getting in the way at all! I'm finishing all my work as always, and I'm making progress in my projects too!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Really? Then when are you getting to sleep every night?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Somewhere around... three or four?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ahem, moving on then.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Given how you're trembling like a baby fowlbeast, I take it you realize the problems this business of yours could cause.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Let's hear it then.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Privately repairing standard-issue equipment without authorization might increase the Engineering Department's maintenance expenses further down the road...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mhm, sounds like you really know your stuff. Who told you that? Jessica?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Instructor Dur-nar reminded me.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Dur-nar?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Glad to hear our old vets still have their priorities straight—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wait, hold up, she told you all that, but didn't bother stopping you? Or even reporting it to me?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Great, sounds like I've another score to settle.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: This has nothing to do with her... It was my own decision.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Do you really have the luxury of worrying about others right now?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Engineering's already overwhelmed with all sorts of orders and requests. This terminal repair thing might be what finally breaks the burdenbeast's back. You get what I'm saying?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: All their metal components originally came from the same batch. Even if some go bad faster or slower, they fall in pretty much the same window. We're already trying to squeeze in time to put together an organized repair-and-replace.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But now, since some of them are fixed but others aren't, that's just one more set of data points for us to wrangle.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I... I have a ledger, and I've kept track of whose terminals I've worked on...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm aware you have the receipts.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But can you guarantee that all the materials used in repairing them came from the same batch?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Which means that to make things more convenient going forward, we'll have to swap them all out again anyway, which is a complete waste of resources!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Sure, we're only talking a few dozen metal components this time, but who knows how big the bill will be next time!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I understand. I know I did wrong...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (I was planning on giving her a stern talking-to, but seeing how obedient she's being, it's hard to find the words...)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Anyway, as the head of Engineering, I'm declaring that as of today, your repair shop is closed indefinitely!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I-I accept your punishment...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: W-Waaah...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Shoot, she seriously started crying... Was I too hard on her?)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: C'mon, stop that. Stop crying.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Blows nose)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So, why did you decide to start doing this in the first place?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I don't have any money, so I can't afford the publication fee...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Publication fee?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wait, didn't I already tell you—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh, I guess I forgot, huh?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Wait, this might be a bitter pill to swallow, but she needs to learn her lesson. Can't let it become water under the bridge that easily.)

spans.text: (Wait, this might be a bitter pill to swallow, but she needs to learn her lesson. Can't let it become water under the bridge

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: In any case, don't do it again.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Let me take a look at your ledger and see how much money you made.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: ...Your net profit was only a thousand LMD?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And you even covered the cost of materials beyond the scope of the request, out-of-pocket?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: AND you waived the entire bill for someone?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: In the end, you fixed up over a hundred items and only made a thousand LMD?!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I was aiming for high volume through low prices, so I set the price at twenty LMD...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There's a floor to how low you can go with that strategy!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I got a mean fifty LMD just from changing out the power cord of the Doctor's kettle while they were busy going through paperwork!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: A power cord doesn't cost that much, does it? Plus, you're basically just plugging it in, aren't you?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ah, ahem. That was simply an example.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Fifty LMD might be a bit overkill for a hot water kettle, but we're talking high-tech terminals here!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Repairing delicate machinery like that means taking them apart with specialized tools and carefully replacing the components. That's gotta be worth at least fifty or sixty!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But back on topic—your paper has basically already been accepted. It only needs some minor tweaks and it's ready to publish.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I was only stopping by to hand you the reviewer's comments when I caught you running a black market repair shop in the dorm hallway.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Wait... What did you just say? My paper... It only needs a few minor revisions?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: This isn't a dream, is it?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Also, I have another piece of good news—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Whispers) I should've told you this first, but better late than never.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You don't have to pay the publication fee either.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Wh-Wh-Wh-What?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm your corresponding author, and Rhodes Island is your employer. Naturally, we'll be covering the fee, so you can stop worrying about breaking the bank.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I can't believe this, I need to pinch myself—

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ow!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Oh my gosh!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ohmygosh, Closure! I'm going to be published!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Waaaah, I'm finally going to be published! My paper is going to be...

spans.text: Waaaah, I'm finally going to be published!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Have you calmed down yet?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Rubs eyes)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Mmhmm!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The publication fee was originally two grand, but I applied for a special hardship grant for you, and managed to get it down to fifteen hundred.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Rhodes Island can easily cover that, so you don't need to stay up all night fixing toasters anymore.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I just realized that, in the end, you're just paying it for me...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah, so?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Um... Isn't that a bit...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: A bit what?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I-I'm thinking that maybe...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Maybe, the publication fee... I...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I think... I should pay it myself after all.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: You and Rhodes Island have been so good to me, but all I've done is give you more work. I'd feel bad taking your money too...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I respect the hustle, but you're still short five hundo.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I can, um, make up the difference by continuing to fix things for people...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Huuuh?!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Not the standard-issue equipment, I promise! I'll stick to fountain pens and water dispensers, I swear!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I know you already let me off easy, and I feel really bad about it!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: But if I accept someone else's charity and use their money to pay the fee without earning it myself, I won't be able to sleep at night!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Snowsant, are you serious?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: (Breathes deeply)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Yes, I'm dead serious.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Can you guarantee it won't get in the way of your work or your research?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I swear it!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You might not even get any business without these terminals, you know.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You sure?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I-I can go around asking everyone if they need anything fixed. I'm sure there'll be someone!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Chuckles wryly)

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, knock yourself out.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Does that mean... I can continue fixing things for people?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What, are you trying to get me to change my mind now?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: N-N-No! Thank you so much, Closure!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But remember to raise your prices. Twenty is lowballing it so much I feel secondhand pain.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I will!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Also, you'd better get your butt in bed by midnight every night.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: That... might be asking a bit much...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's not up for negotiation. If anyone else gets sick, I'll give them sick leave; but if you get sick... I'm cutting your wages!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Noooo! Fine, I understand!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: One last thing. I overheard you and Jessica talking about how you managed to simplify the design and bypass the metal component?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Do you have a blueprint? Let me take a look.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mhm...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, I'll be. That's just crazy enough to work.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Snowsant, I'm going to take this with me and look into it a bit more, maybe make a few improvements. If all goes well, you'll be in charge of rolling out the standardized updates for all our terminals.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Huh? You're... putting me in charge?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It's your blueprint, your idea, your hours of lost sleep. Who else would be in charge?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Also, this approach is pretty novel. After you make some progress with your work, keep looking into it. Who knows, maybe you've already got a second paper on your hands?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: A-A-A second paper?!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: C-Closure! I-Isn't it a bit early to think about my second paper when my first still hasn't been published?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: And what's wrong with that? If you've got the ability and the work ethic, why shouldn't your hard work be rewarded?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright, go celebrate with Jessica. I've still got a meeting to get to, so I can't join you.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh, and before I forget again, here's the letter from the reviewer!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Bye bye!

a.text: The manuscript you submitted to this journal (No. 011224) has passed preliminary review, but also requires certain revisions.

The reviewer's comments are attached to this letter. Please submit the revised manuscript to the editorial board before the deadline. If you have any other questions, please feel free to contact the board. Thank you for your dedication to theoretical research!
The shortcomings of this paper are obvious.

The author is unaware of the latest breakthroughs in this field, and often runs into the problem of 'reinventing the wheel' in regards to theoretical derivations; experimental design is excessively rigid with a focus on theory over practice, ignoring the applications of new technologies in the field, etc.
However, the author's originality, sensitivity to practical issues, and meticulous thoughtfulness in laying out the argument are all admirable.
Above all, the author has overcome many of the aforementioned problems with a degree of perseverance and diligence far beyond most people, which has impressed us deeply.
We hope that the author will continue to maintain this diligence and venture ever further on the road of academia.
